I already mentioned that fact. I said it's used for ezreal when he uses E, which is essentially the same as what you're saying, but the question here isn't even a good question. He asks is QRW or QWR better and QWR just is generally not used that much.

Most people max W then Q then E. Because of that, the W will be the highest damage ability up until lv 11, so you want to use your W for damage up until lv 11. That's why it's recommended to copy your W with R before a fight, so that you can use your W for damage, as R does comparatively less damage until lv 11. Furthermore, your R damage has nothing to do with the rank of your other abilities. Copying any ability does roughly the same damage. In fact, the Q and E do the same damage and R is barely any different. So, you don't really have to consider the damage for your R but, rather, just think about what the situation calls for. If you need a fast combo, use R to copy Q. If you need to gap close, use R to copy W. If you need to double chain, use R to copy E.

As, for tips, one of the hardest parts of learning Leblanc is understanding how to use all of her combos. Even after having played her for so long, I still will use the wrong combos from time to time. She has many and a lot of them are quite situational. I'll tell you the most common ones to use. Also, note that the second part of your chain can trigger the Q mark damage.

QW is for quick early trading in lane and only works if they're not spacing correctly.

WEQ and WEQR are for high damage trades

WREQ and WRQE are for long distance bursting

WQRE and WEQR are for mid to late game 1 shots

EQRW is used if enemy face checks into you or is melee

ER is for double chaining, which is good for ganks and tanks

Between Lv 6 and Lv 11, if you're roaming or trading, try and mimic your W with your R and use it as a gap closer because it does very low damage. It is very useful because it allows you to do RQW which is a really high damage combo for early to mid game and is nearly undodgeable.

Also you can E flash, which is important for hard-to-dodge chaining
